newsitem.title: INDONESIA: FOCUS-Rupiah plunges,dealers look for intervention.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Rupiah plunges,dealers look for intervention.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah plunged further on Friday, the day after it was floated, and dealers said they were looking to the central bank to intervene and restore market confidence.

The rupiah fell to a new record low of 2,915 to the dollar by early afternoon from its opening level of 2,770/90 after liquidity suddenly eased from a record overnight rate of 125 percent to about 30 percent.
The overnight rate determines whether it is profitable for investors to borrow rupiah to speculate in the foreign exchange market.

"At this rate, borrowing costs are just about five rupiah (per dollar). It's extremely profitable for people to speculate, since there are swings of about 100 rupiah in the spot rate," said one dealer.
Edwin Png, head of treasury for Bank of America in Jakarta, said the market was losing confidence.
"I have housewives calling me up to ask about the rate," he said. "Bank Indonesia should intervene now or else I see the rate going up to 3,000 later in the day and 3,200 next week.
"They should do both. They should intervene and they should tighten liquidity."

Other dealers said the easing in liquidity appeared to have come about after some state-owned banks offered money in the market and added that that implied the central bank was being inconsistent in its policy.
"They said yesterday that they would maintain tightness, but it doesn't look as if they are doing so," said one dealer.
The overnight rate shot up in the morning because of Bank Indonesia's intervention on Wednesday with about $500 million. The money became due on Friday.

Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said on Thursday, less than an hour after the central bank removed its intervention band and effectively floated the rupiah, that tight monetary and fiscal policies were in place and any changes would depend on developments.

Central Bank Governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said although the intervention band had been scrapped, authorities reserved the right to intervene if they deemed necessary. The band had determined at what levels the bank would step into the market.
"Of course Bank Indonesia would like to intervene to keep developments on course, to smooth the adaptment period," he said on Thursday.
But State Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita appeared to hint that authorities would allow the market to decide the level of the rupiah.
"If they (speculators) see the government will not intervene, we hope they will reduce their speculative activity," he told reporters on Friday.
"Our fundamental economy is sound. We are entering a new era of market principles. It is the correct time for the government to carry out such a policy," he said.
Earlier, the International Monetary Fund hailed the move to float the rupiah, saying it was good for the economy.

"In present circumstances, a floating exchange rate will enhance the effectiveness of macroeconomic policies aimed at sustaining high rates of growth with financial stability," said Stanley Fischer, acting managing director of the IMF, in a statement issued in Washington.
